import pandas as pd

# Get trip data and compute pooled share by day and class
trips = tables['trips']

# Filter for season 6, recent days (d130-d151 to see the recent trend)
s6_trips = trips[trips['fished_date_season'] == 6].copy()
recent_trips = s6_trips[(s6_trips['fished_date_doy'] >= 130) & (s6_trips['fished_date_doy'] <= 151)].copy()

# Group by day and class, sum yt and anglers
daily_class = recent_trips.groupby(['fished_date_doy', 'cls']).agg({
    'yt': 'sum',
    'anglers': 'sum'
}).reset_index()

# Calculate share per day per class
daily_class['pooled_share'] = daily_class['yt'] / daily_class['anglers']

# Pivot to see by day
pivot = daily_class.pivot(index='fished_date_doy', columns='cls', values='pooled_share').fillna(0)

print("Pooled share by day and class (d130-d151):")
print(pivot.to_string())
print("\n")

# Look for streaks: 3+ consecutive days in any class >1.0 avg
print("Looking for 3+ day streaks >1.0 avg:")
for cls in pivot.columns:
    series = pivot[cls]
    days = series[series > 1.0].index.tolist()
    if len(days) > 0:
        print(f"\n{cls}: positive days = {sorted(days)}")
        # Check for consecutive runs
        for i, day in enumerate(sorted(days)):
            if i > 0:
                streak_start = sorted(days)[max(0, i-2)]
                if day - sorted(days)[i-1] == 1:
                    print(f"  Potential streak starting d{streak_start}")

# Show latest 5 days with all classes
print("\nLatest 5 days (d147-d151):")
print(pivot.tail(5))
